storylines.title: Dalen Terry, Thunder Agree To Two-Year Contract
storylines.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder and veteran wing Dalen Terry have agreed to a two-year contract. Terry will fill the Thunder's open roster spot and will give the team some much needed depth. Last season, Terry split the campaign between the Chicago Bulls and Philadelphia 76ers. Terry was traded by the Bulls to the New York Knicks at the trade deadline, then he signed a two-way contract with the Sixers. From there, the 6-foot-7 wing signed a standard contract with Philadelphia. The Thunder are currently down six players due to injuries. That includes Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, who are expected to miss the remainder of the season, and Chet Holmgren who is out for 8-10 weeks.

storylines.title: Seven Players See 27-28 Rookie Scale Team Options Declined
storylines.summary: The deadline for NBA teams to exercise rookie scale team options for the 2027-28 season was Monday, November 2. Normally this deadline is October 31, but as that day fell on a weekend, it shifted back to Monday. Seven players did not have their rookie scale scale team options picked up: Isaiah Collier - Utah Jazz: $4.8 million fourth-year option Pacome Dadiet - New York Knicks: $5.4 million fourth-year option DaRon Holmes II - Denver Nuggets: $5.5 million fourth-year option A.J. Johnson - New Orleans Pelicans: $5.5 million fourth-year option Tidjane Salaun - Charlotte Hornets: $10.4 million fourth-year option Nikola Topic - Oklahoma City Thunder: $7.5 million fourth-year option Cody Williams - Minnesota Timberwolves: $7.6 million fourth-year option
